The approved variant (C) is in `reference-renders/` (its WAVs also remain here). The renders can be regenerated with the round script named in `dog5-docs/voicing/README.md` (some need the pre-change base tree). The README below is generated; it still lists the removed files.

# 31 Fi(l)fth — voicing round (Batch 1A, the attack set)

*Generated by tests/voicing/batch01a.py. Level-matched to the bank reference (−18.0 dBFS RMS, note-on region) on phrase (b) FIFTH-BASED STABS; the bank's own phrase (b) is in the table as well. Every parameter change is before → after under the echo rule in numbers.md.*

**Recommended: B centre** — a POLY stab with the fifth built into every voice (OSC 2 +7 st): fast pluck from the filter envelope (1850 Hz at the attack → 912 Hz, +6.8 dB snap), a short 89 ms slap behind it, 288 ms to −60 dB with the repeats (72 ms voice alone), CPU 1075 worst-case host instr/sample (idle 380 + load 695) against C's 1765 worst-case host instr/sample (idle 380 + load 1384). C (DUAL) is fatter (40% under 150 Hz vs 32%) but doubles the cost and the chord needs six voices; D only lengthens the echo.

## What to listen to

`*_riff.wav` (single notes = a fifth in every note: the real test of this patch) and `*_stabs.wav` (the pilot's fifth-based chords: a
fifth on every note of an already-fifth chord stacks into a sus2 cluster, so judge chord body on the riff rather than on the stabs).
Listen for: the pluck against the sustain, the slap's size, whether B is fat enough or C is needed.

*Notes.* Phrase (b)'s chords already contain fifths, so +7 st stacks them (E+B becomes E, B, B, F#): that is the engine doing what the patch asks.
The level is read on (b) as for every patch. Variant A is the MONO fifths lead this slot was (rendered through the base program path).
